request: Create a skid buffer with valid/ready handshakes.
expected_behavior: RTL for module skid_buffer (a register slice on a valid/ready stream, WIDTH-bit beats with WIDTH 8 by default and any WIDTH from 1 allowed) with s_valid, s_ready and s_data upstream, m_valid, m_ready and m_data downstream, every output driven from a flop, full throughput with one beat in and one out per cycle, room for one more beat while the output stalls, and a self-checking testbench, following the approved interface specification and microarchitecture, gated by lint, simulation, and synthesis (and formal, when a .sby is written) before review.
constraints: Work only from the approved interface specification and microarchitecture.
Correct for every WIDTH from 1 up: the control does not depend on the data width.
s_ready, m_valid and m_data come from flops: no combinational path from m_ready or s_valid to an output.
Lint-clean under Verilator -Wall with no waivers.
known_failure_modes: A beat accepted in the cycle the output stalls that is overwritten or dropped.
s_ready computed from m_ready, which lengthens the timing path the slice exists to cut.
A beat sent twice when ready rises after a stall, or the skid beat sent after a newer one.
m_data that changes while m_valid is high and m_ready low.
A slice that takes a beat only every other cycle, losing full throughput.
A self-written testbench that never stalls the output with a beat already held; the held-out reference testbench judges instead.
A self-written testbench that cannot tell a dropped skid beat, a combinational ready, a duplicated beat or unstable output data from a correct slice; the must-fail control fails it.

held_out.name: The reference testbench passes on the seat's RTL
The seat's testbench fails each skid buffer mutant
The case's WIDTH 8 proof reaches every cover and fails each mutant
The case's WIDTH 1 proof reaches every cover and fails each mutant
